title: Federal Register: Renewal of an Approved Information Collection Request, Commercial Driver's License Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse (OMB 2126-0057)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, FMCSA (via GovInfo / Federal Register)
source_type: Government Paperwork Reduction Act information collection notice (30-day)
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency (FMCSA) is also the party imposing and administering the requirement. The burden figure is the agency's estimate for an OMB renewal.
findings: FMCSA estimates 9,834,949 respondents (motor carriers, drivers, MROs, SAPs, C/TPAs, SDLAs), 10 to 20 minutes per response, and an estimated total annual burden of 1,653,032 hours; the prior approval was set to expire August 31, 2026.

Employers or their C/TPAs must query the Clearinghouse for each currently employed driver at least once a year and for prospective employees as needed; employer reports are due by the close of the third business day after the employer obtains the information.

The notice says 88 comments were received (71 by the June 1, 2026 deadline); it says the comments suggested regulatory changes (for example SAP access to complete driver histories) and did not directly address the published costs or burden hours.
The notice states the compliance date was January 6, 2020 and registration began in September 2019.
limitations: This is a renewal notice; it does not break burden out by carrier size, does not mention owner-operators, and gives no per-carrier hours.
The renewed approval status by OMB after the 30-day period was not checked.
The 60-day notice (91 FR 16278, April 1, 2026) was skimmed only for the same headline figures and is not recorded as a separate source.
